items.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I also was able to tune in the Voice of America with Willis Conover and that’s where I heard a huge amount of the great jazz that I became so familiar with.

ctx.x: This man was a D.J., not a band leader.

Yeah. No he was a D.J. It was amazing because a daunting sort of task he must have had every day, because he would have conversations between the record that he played, he’d maybe play a conversation out of a radio drama, it might be “The Whistler,” and he would have a conversation with tape. It must have taken him all day, because in those days it was slicing with a razor blade, right, to edit tape. It was great, it was great, it was a lot of fun. Wow. You came all the way over here. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
